definitions.explanation: The Japanese period mark (。) placed at the end of a sentence. One of the basic punctuation marks in Japanese writing.

examples.english: Place a period at the end of a sentence.

examples.japanese: {句点|くてん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{使|つか}い{方|かた}→使い方：07797_tsukaikata⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{習|なら}った→習う：00479_narau⟧。
examples.english: I learned how to use periods and commas.

examples.japanese: ⟦メッセージ→メッセージ：03828_messeeji⟧⟦アプリ→アプリ：04722_apuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{句点|くてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}けない→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: More and more people don't use periods in messaging apps.

notes: The Japanese period is 。(a small circle), not a dot like in English. Common collocations: {句点|くてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ (to put a period), {句点|くてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{付|つ}ける→付ける：00761_tsukeru⟧ (to add a period). The pair of {句点|くてん} (period) and ⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧ (comma、) are together called ⟦{句読点|くとうてん}→句読点：08650_kutouten⟧ (punctuation marks). In modern messaging, younger Japanese speakers often omit {句点|くてん} in casual texts, as ending with 。 can feel cold or distant.
